attacks.attack: 1. Claim erasure but secretly retain the content
attacks.detail: C2 (the erasure record) is witnessed=True; witnesses confirm a signed Certificate of Destruction was appended + ordered + co-signed — they cannot see inside custody. Proving the bytes are physically gone needs HSM/enclave attestation, a separate gate. P1-03 upgrades 'operator's word' to 'independently witnessed record', not to physical-destruction proof.
attacks.verdict: ACCEPTED LIMIT — witnesses attest the RECORD, not physical destruction (enclave gate)

attacks.attack: 2. Repudiate: deny the erasure ever happened
attacks.detail: the erasure checkpoint is co-signed by 3 independent witnesses (witnessed=True); the operator cannot later claim it never happened — k independent parties recorded it.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — a witnessed C2 is non-repudiable

attacks.attack: 3. Forge a witnessed erasure with operator-controlled keys
attacks.detail: k operator-signed 'witness' anchors -> valid=[], witnessed=False. The operator cannot manufacture a witnessed erasure without real witnesses.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — pinned registry rejects operator-minted witnesses

attacks.attack: 4. Un-erase: roll back to before the certificate
attacks.detail: presenting the size-10 pre-erasure log against witnessed C2 (size 11) -> detected=True. The witnessed erasure checkpoint can't be undone unseen.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — can't shrink below a witnessed C2

attacks.attack: 5. Backdate the erasure (claim an earlier time)
attacks.detail: consistency enforces that the erasure was appended AFTER C1 (ordering can't be forged); but the recorded erased_at is operator-set and witness-observed — a precise real-world time needs an external time-anchor / VDF (carried from RUN 04).
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED (ordering, after C1) + ACCEPTED LIMIT (exact wall-clock needs a time-anchor)

attacks.detail: over-claim hits: none; discloses not-physical-destruction: True; discloses G3 collusion: True.
attacks.verdict: DEFENDED — discloses the physical-destruction and >=k-collusion limits
